organizations.canonical_name: United States Army, Film Branch, Special Service Division
organizations.normalization_notes: Modeled from the unit name printed in the March 1943 YANK article. The article says most personnel were attached to the 834th Signal Company, but it does not state that Arnoldy personally held that company assignment, so the organizations are not merged.

affiliations.date_precision: YANK documents the film advisory work in its 5 March 1943 issue; a scholarly chronology places Arnoldy in the OSS Yugoslav Desk by December 1943. Exact start, end, and transfer dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact uncommon name and major rank align across the index, contemporary Army article, archival OSS interview index, and scholarly OSS chronology. The March-to-December sequence makes the Film Branch the best-supported predecessor located so far, but no source explicitly says Arnoldy transferred directly from it to OSS. The assignment is military, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Francis N. Arnoldy is the Army film adviser later documented as OSS Yugoslav Desk chief at Bari.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA row, contemporary Army article, archival interview index, and scholarly OSS chronology align on an uncommon name, major rank, Army context, Bari station, and OSS role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name plus compatible major rank in three records, a contemporary Army assignment, a Bari archival entry, and a direct OSS Yugoslav Desk chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army article is dated 5 March 1943; the dissertation places Arnoldy in the OSS Yugoslav Desk from December 1943 to July 1944.
claims.match_notes: Box 22 remains unreviewed, so the identity is not promoted to confirmed. A postwar Berlin military-government listing and family references were reviewed only as corroborative leads and are not used for this pre-OSS conclusion.

claims.claim_text: Francis N. Arnoldy's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation is a U.S. Army Film Branch assignment as technical adviser on Russian films.
claims.evidence_excerpt: He was technical advisor on the Russian films.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary Army article places Major Arnoldy in the Film Branch as a Russian-film adviser in March 1943; a scholarly source dates his OSS desk leadership from December 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the uncommon name, major rank, Army role, Bari archival entry, and direct OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate: the documented Film Branch work precedes the documented OSS appointment by nine months, but the reviewed sources do not exclude an intervening assignment or state an explicit transfer.
claims.match_notes: Published as a qualified military predecessor and excluded from confirmed/high-only aggregate charts. It is not a civilian-employer finding. Box 22 is needed to establish the exact transfer sequence.

sources.excerpt_override: He was technical advisor on the Russian films.
